plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and frost, making it one of the earliest signs of the end of winter in temperate gardens and woodlands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Native to Europe; widely naturalized in the UK, Northern Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce a compound called galantamine, which is used in medication to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that bears fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in the depths of winter. It is highly prized in East Asian gardens, bonsai, and art, and is followed by sour fruits used for pickling and liqueur.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: In Chinese culture the plum blossom is one of the 'Three Friends of Winter' and symbolizes perseverance and hope because it blooms in the cold.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across, made of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny flowers. It thrives in the fynbos vegetation on nutrient-poor, acidic soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mostly late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with some blooms in late summer and autumn; flowering cultivars can appear in February
plants.location: Southwestern and southern Cape regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The King Protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its lineage is ancient, dating back tens of millions of years.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that bloom in winter. It is popular in woodland gardens and mild-winter regions, with thousands of cultivars varying in form from single to fully double.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and hair care.
